subject: math.AG
name: Hodge conjecture
statement: For every smooth projective complex variety X, is each rational cohomology class of type (p,p) a rational linear combination of classes of codimension-p algebraic cycles?
importance: Would identify exactly which cohomology classes arise from algebraic subvarieties.
status_note: The rational formulation remains open in general; the corresponding integral statement is false.

subject: math.AG
name: Tate conjecture for cycles over finite fields
statement: For a smooth projective variety X over a finite field and a prime ℓ different from its characteristic, do algebraic codimension-r cycles span the Frobenius-invariant subspace of H_et^{2r}(X_bar,Q_ℓ(r))?
importance: Links algebraic cycles to arithmetic symmetries and zeta functions.
status_note: Many divisor and special-variety cases are proved; arbitrary varieties and codimensions are open.

subject: math.AG
name: Lefschetz standard conjecture
statement: For every smooth projective variety X and a Weil cohomology theory, is the inverse of each hard-Lefschetz isomorphism induced by an algebraic correspondence?
importance: Would make the Lefschetz decomposition algebraic and underpin the theory of pure motives.
status_note: Known for many varieties, including abelian varieties; the unrestricted algebraic-correspondence statement is open.

subject: math.AG
name: Hodge standard conjecture
statement: For every smooth projective variety X of dimension n over an arbitrary field, a fixed Weil cohomology theory, and an ample class L, is the pairing (a,b) ↦ (−1)^r deg(a·b·L^{n−2r}) positive definite on rational primitive algebraic cohomology classes of codimension r≤n/2?
importance: Would provide the positivity needed for a semisimple and well-behaved theory of motives.
status_note: The characteristic-zero complex case follows from Hodge theory; the conjecture over fields of positive characteristic remains open in general.

subject: math.AG
name: Abundance conjecture
statement: If (X,Δ) is a projective klt pair over a field of characteristic zero with Δ a Q-divisor and K_X+Δ nef, must K_X+Δ be semiample?
importance: Would complete the passage from minimal models to canonical fibrations.
status_note: Established in low dimensions and important special cases; arbitrary dimension is open.

subject: math.AG
name: Termination of flips
statement: For a projective klt pair (X,Δ) in characteristic zero, must every sequence of (K_X+Δ)-flips terminate?
importance: Would guarantee that the birational minimal-model procedure eventually finishes.
status_note: Termination is known under additional hypotheses and in low dimensions; unrestricted sequences in arbitrary dimension remain open.

subject: math.AG
name: Nagata conjecture
statement: For r≥10 nonsquare very general points of P^2_C, must every plane curve of degree d having multiplicity at least m at all points satisfy d ≥ m√r?
importance: Determines expected asymptotic positivity on blowups of the projective plane.
status_note: Square values of r are proved; nonsquare values remain open. Special configurations need not obey this bound.

subject: math.AG
name: Jacobian conjecture in dimension two
statement: Over a characteristic-zero field k, is every polynomial map F:k^2 → k^2 whose Jacobian determinant is a nonzero constant a polynomial automorphism?
importance: Asks whether an infinitesimal invertibility condition forces global polynomial invertibility.
status_note: The two-dimensional characteristic-zero problem remains open. Reported 2026 counterexamples in dimensions greater than two rule out listing the former all-dimensional conjecture as open.

references.title: Counterexamples to the Jacobian conjecture in dimensions greater than two

subject: math.AG
name: Grothendieck section conjecture
statement: For a smooth projective geometrically connected curve X of genus at least two over a number field k, is the map from X(k) to conjugacy classes of continuous sections of π_1(X) → Gal(k_bar/k) bijective?
importance: Would recover rational points from the arithmetic fundamental group.
status_note: The curve and number-field hypotheses are essential; the full bijection remains open.

subject: math.AG
name: Zariski cancellation for affine three-space in characteristic zero
statement: If A is a finitely generated commutative integral C-algebra and A[t] is isomorphic to C[x_1,x_2,x_3,x_4], must A be isomorphic to C[x_1,x_2,x_3]?
importance: Asks whether an affine factor can be uniquely recovered after adjoining one coordinate.
status_note: Cancellation is known in lower dimension and fails in positive characteristic; the characteristic-zero three-space case remains open.

references.title: Gupta, A survey on Zariski cancellation problem
